extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark of 1,500 human-selected samples designed to evaluate large vision-language models with purified, visually dependent questions. It covers 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes and is intended to measure actual multi-modal capacity while reducing data leakage and text-only shortcuts.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark samples were first preliminarily filtered using an automated pipeline with closed-source and open-source LLM inspectors, then manually reviewed by three experts to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and advanced multi-modal difficulty; 1,500 high-quality samples were finally curated from the filtered pool.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples were collected from two benchmarks focused on natural images and four benchmarks centered on scientific and technical knowledge, with an initial pool of 22,401 samples reduced to 11,607 after filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, three experts conducted manual review to ensure each sample was based on visual content, covered capability dimensions, and required advanced multi-modal abilities; samples were also organized into difficulty categories using hit counts from 16 LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality/selection analysis used hit counts from 16 LVLMs and retained samples with two or fewer hits; around 75% of LLM inspectors failed to answer correctly.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs (20B or larger) were used as inspectors with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may be biased toward samples that are vision-critical and toward tasks/dimensions selected after filtering out items answerable by text-only LLMs or potentially leaked into models, which could affect representativeness of broader multimodal evaluation data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies two main limitations in existing benchmarks: many samples do not require visual content, and some samples may be unintentionally leaked into LLM/LVLM training data. It also notes that MMStar is a benchmark for evaluation rather than general-purpose training, and plans to expand it into a larger online test set to maintain visual dependency and reduce accidental leakage.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve the accuracy of multimodal model evaluation and avoid misjudging model capability, which may better guide future LVLM research and benchmark construction.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Used as a vision-dependent multimodal benchmark for evaluation/testing of LVLMs, including measuring accuracy, multi-modal gain (MG), and multi-modal leakage (ML). The authors also mention future expansion into an online test set for dynamic evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states a future plan to expand MMStar into a larger online test set and use dynamic evaluation methods to maintain visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage; no explicit maintainer or deprecation policy is given.

name.evidence: we present MMStar, an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans.

description.evidence: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.

inLanguage.evidence: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have recently achieved rapid progress

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “we employ two closed-source LLMs ... and six open-source LLMs ... to serve as inspectors” and “After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process” and “Finally ... we manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples from the coarsely filtered set.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process” and “we manually curated 1,500 high-quality samples”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “We first choose two benchmarks [27, 21] focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge [51, 30, 20, 29] for our sample collection.” and “our sample pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607.”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample’s answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “we evaluate the sample pool with these LLM inspectors, documenting the hit frequency for each evaluation sample. Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits, indicating that around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer.”

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: “we employ two closed-source LLMs [41, 34] and six open-source LLMs [1, 42, 49, 3, 19, 43] sizing 20B or larger to serve as inspectors. These open-source LLMs are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded as they may exist leaking or visual-unnecessary problems.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “visual content is unnecessary for many samples” and “unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “The existence of inappropriate questions and data leaking would lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “we develop an elite vision-dependent multi-modal benchmark named MMStar and propose two metrics to measure the data leakage and actual performance gain”

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: “In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage”
